events.note: Reid signed a two-year contract extension with Fremantle in June 2025, taking him from the end of 2027 through to the end of 2029, after an impressive debut season.

events.name: Murphy Reid
events.note: Reid signed a three-year contract extension with Fremantle, taking him from the end of 2029 through to the end of 2032 and to free agency, after winning the Rising Star and the Glendinning-Allan Medal.

events.name: Tom Stewart
events.note: Stewart re-signed with Geelong beyond his initial deal, locking him in until the end of 2019.

events.name: Tom Stewart
events.note: Stewart signed a new deal adding three years to his existing contract (which ran to 2021), keeping him at Geelong until the end of 2024.

events.name: Tom Stewart
events.note: Stewart signed a three-year contract extension keeping him at Geelong until the end of 2027, cementing him as a 'Cat for life'.

events.name: Adam Cerra
events.note: As an 18-year-old, Cerra signed a two-year contract extension with Fremantle, committing him to the club until at least the end of the 2021 season.

events.name: Adam Cerra
events.note: After requesting a trade out of Fremantle, Cerra was traded to Carlton (on his 22nd birthday) in exchange for pick No.6 in the 2021 draft and a future third-round selection.

events.name: Adam Cerra
events.note: Cerra signed a five-year contract extension with Carlton, committing him to the club until at least the end of the 2030 season.

events.name: Jacob Weitering
events.note: Weitering signed a four-year contract extension, announced at the John Nicholls Medal, keeping him at Carlton until at least the end of 2021.

events.name: Jacob Weitering
events.note: Weitering signed a four-year extension with one year still to run on his prior deal, committing him to Carlton until the end of 2025.

events.name: Jacob Weitering
events.note: Weitering signed a six-year extension with a year still remaining on his contract, committing him to Carlton until at least the end of 2031.

events.name: Bailey Humphrey
events.note: After just eight games and Rising Star buzz, Humphrey signed a four-year contract extension with Gold Coast, replacing his original two-year deal and locking him in through the end of the 2028 season.

events.name: John Noble
events.note: Noble signed a two-year contract extension with Collingwood, keeping him at the club through the end of 2023.

events.name: John Noble
events.note: Off the back of a career-best 2023 season, Noble signed a new three-year contract extension locking him in at Collingwood until the end of 2026.

events.name: John Noble
events.note: Noble was traded from Collingwood to Gold Coast as part of a three-club mega trade also involving Port Adelaide, joining the Suns on a new four-year contract through the end of 2028.

events.name: Sam Taylor
events.note: Taylor signed a two-year contract extension keeping him at GWS until the end of 2022.

events.name: Sam Taylor
events.note: Taylor signed a three-year contract extension, tying him to GWS until at least the end of 2025.

events.name: Sam Taylor
events.note: Taylor signed a seven-year contract extension, one of the longest deals in AFL history, keeping him at GWS until at least the end of 2032.

events.name: Blake Hardwick
events.note: Signed a two-year contract extension keeping him at Hawthorn until at least the end of 2019, after a breakout 2017 season and a Round 15 Rising Star nomination.

events.name: Blake Hardwick
events.note: Re-signed for a further two years to 2021 after a breakout 2018 season (24 games) that saw him finish runner-up in the Peter Crimmins Medal.

events.name: Blake Hardwick
events.note: Signed a new long-term deal to remain at Hawthorn until at least the end of 2024.

events.name: Blake Hardwick
events.note: Turned down free agency to sign a five-year contract extension, keeping him at Hawthorn until at least the end of 2029.

events.name: Justin McInerney
events.note: McInerney, then 21, signed a four-year contract extension keeping him at Sydney until at least the end of 2026.

events.name: Justin McInerney
events.note: McInerney, then 25, signed a five-year extension taking his name off the free agency list and committing him to Sydney through the end of 2031.

events.name: Jack Bowes
events.note: Bowes signed a long-term extension with Gold Coast, committing through the end of 2024 (a heavily back-ended five-year deal).

events.name: Jack Bowes
events.note: Gold Coast traded Bowes (with pick 7) to Geelong for a future third-round pick as part of a salary-cap 'salary dump' deal; Bowes committed to a new four-year contract with the Cats, running through 2026.

events.name: Brayden Maynard
events.note: Signed a two-year contract extension through to the end of the 2020 season.

events.name: Brayden Maynard
events.note: Turned down eligibility for free agency at end of 2022 to sign a three-year extension through to the end of 2025.

events.name: Brayden Maynard
events.note: As an unrestricted free agent, rejected interest from North Melbourne and other rivals to re-sign with Collingwood on a four-year deal through to the end of 2029.

events.name: Jeremy Howe
events.note: Traded from Melbourne to Collingwood in a four-club, day-six 2015 trade period deal (Pies sent Paul Seedsman and Ben Kennedy the other way, along with pick 68, for Howe).

events.name: Jeremy Howe
events.reporter: Collingwood FC (collingwoodfc.com.au), "Howe signs on for three"
events.note: Signed a three-year contract extension with Collingwood, tying him to the club until the end of the 2021 season.

events.name: Jeremy Howe
events.note: Added another year to his existing deal, locking him in at Collingwood until the end of 2022 (alongside Jamie Elliott).

events.name: Jeremy Howe
events.note: Signed a one-year extension on the eve of the 2023 season, committing him to Collingwood through the end of 2024.

events.name: Jeremy Howe
events.note: Signed a one-year extension to play on in 2025, his 10th season at Collingwood.

events.name: Jeremy Howe
events.reporter: Collingwood FC (collingwoodfc.com.au), "Sidebottom and Howe sign on"
events.note: Signed a one-year extension (announced late August 2025) alongside Steele Sidebottom to play a 16th AFL season in 2026.

events.name: Jack Ginnivan
events.note: Ginnivan signed a two-year contract extension with Collingwood, announced alongside teammates Nathan Kreuger/Ruscoe.

events.name: Jack Ginnivan
events.note: Ginnivan was traded from Collingwood to Hawthorn on the final day of the 2023 AFL Trade Period, with clubs swapping second-round picks and Collingwood also receiving a future third-round selection.

events.name: Jack Ginnivan
events.note: On joining Hawthorn via trade, Ginnivan signed a four-year deal, three years longer than what remained on his Collingwood contract; Hawthorn's own site lists him as contracted until 2027.

events.name: Sam Flanders
events.note: Signed a two-year contract extension with Gold Coast, tying him to the club through the end of 2023.

events.name: Sam Flanders
events.note: Signed a four-year contract extension with Gold Coast through to the end of 2027, announced live on stage at the club's Best Emerging Player award night.

events.name: Sam Flanders
events.note: Traded from Gold Coast to St Kilda during the AFL Trade Period, with the Saints sending Pick 7 in the 2025 National Draft to the Suns; reported to have signed a new long-term deal with St Kilda as part of the move.

events.name: Bailey Williams
events.note: Signed a two-year contract extension keeping him at the Western Bulldogs until at least the end of 2019.

events.name: Bailey Williams
events.note: Re-signed with the Western Bulldogs on a two-year extension, committing him to the club until at least the end of 2021.

events.name: Bailey Williams
events.note: Signed a two-year extension with the Western Bulldogs, taking him from a 2021 expiry to at least the end of 2023.

events.name: Bailey Williams
events.note: Recommitted to the Western Bulldogs on a four-year extension, keeping him at the club until at least the end of the 2027 season.

events.name: Beau McCreery
events.note: McCreery signed a three-year contract extension with Collingwood, announced alongside John Noble and Jakob Ryan re-signing, keeping him at the club until at least the end of 2027. Exact day of the announcement wasn't stated on the page (July 2023 per corroborating coverage), so the date is estimated to mid-month.

events.name: Tom De Koning
events.note: De Koning signed a two-year contract extension with Carlton, keeping him at the club until at least the end of 2025, turning down rival interest.

events.name: Tom De Koning
events.note: De Koning left Carlton as a restricted free agent (Carlton chose not to match St Kilda's offer) and signed a reported eight-year deal with St Kilda, officially joining when free agency opened on 3 October 2025.

events.name: James Peatling
events.note: Peatling signed a two-year contract extension with GWS, tying him to the Giants until the end of 2024.

events.name: James Peatling
events.note: Traded from GWS to Adelaide on the final day of the 2024 AFL Trade Period; Adelaide sent a future second-round pick for Peatling plus future third- and fourth-round selections.

events.name: James Peatling
events.reporter: Tom Morris (Channel 9 / Trade Radio) via X
events.note: Alongside the trade, Peatling signed a four-year contract with Adelaide, running through the end of 2028.

events.name: Rory Lobb
events.note: Lobb signed a two-year contract extension with GWS, rejecting interest from WA clubs, keeping him at the Giants through the end of 2019.

events.name: Rory Lobb
events.note: Traded from GWS to Fremantle on the final day of the 2018 trade period (GWS received picks 11 and 19; Fremantle gave up Lobb plus picks 14, 43 and 47); Lobb signed a four-year deal running from 2019 to 2022.

events.name: Rory Lobb
events.note: Traded from Fremantle to the Western Bulldogs (Bulldogs gave up pick 30 in the 2022 draft and a future second-round pick) and signed a four-year contract through to the end of 2026.

events.name: Rory Lobb
events.note: Lobb signed a further contract extension with the Western Bulldogs, adding a season and keeping him at the club through the end of 2027, amid career-best form as a key defender.

events.name: Jaspa Fletcher
events.note: Fletcher signed a two-year contract extension with Brisbane, keeping him at the club until the end of the 2026 season, after a strong debut 2023 campaign that included a Round 19 Rising Star nomination.

events.name: Jaspa Fletcher
events.note: Having already been contracted through 2026, Fletcher signed a further four-year extension with Brisbane, taking his deal through to the end of 2030, shortly after the club's 2025 premiership.

events.name: Bradley Hill
events.note: Hill signed a one-year contract extension with Hawthorn in September 2013, tying him to the club until the end of 2015.

events.name: Bradley Hill
events.note: After an outstanding start to the 2014 season, Hawthorn re-signed Hill on a new deal locking him in until the end of 2017.

events.name: Bradley Hill
events.note: Traded from Hawthorn to Fremantle (Hawthorn received pick 23 in the 2016 NAB AFL Draft) so Hill could return to Western Australia and play alongside brother Stephen Hill.

events.name: Bradley Hill
events.note: On joining Fremantle via trade from Hawthorn, Hill signed a five-year contract; a 2018 club article confirmed he was contracted at Fremantle until at least the end of the 2021 season.

events.name: Bradley Hill
events.note: Traded from Fremantle to St Kilda on the final day of the 2019 Trade Period, with St Kilda sending Blake Acres, picks 10 and 58, and future selections to Fremantle for Hill.

events.name: Bradley Hill
events.note: Upon arriving at St Kilda via trade from Fremantle, Hill signed a five-year contract with the Saints.

events.name: Bradley Hill
events.reporter: National Indigenous Times / Canberra Times / St Kilda FC
events.note: Ahead of his 250th AFL game, Hill signed a three-year contract extension with St Kilda, committing him to the club until at least the end of the 2027 season.

events.name: Mark Keane
events.note: After leaving Collingwood (delisted/uncontracted following a stint back in Ireland during Covid), Keane signed a one-year deal with Adelaide during the pre-season supplemental signing period.

events.name: Mark Keane
events.note: Keane turned down interest from Victorian clubs, including a return to former club Collingwood, and signed a three-year contract extension keeping him at Adelaide until at least the end of 2028.

events.name: Jack Buckley
events.note: Upgraded from Category B rookie to the primary list with a two-year contract after his 2020 AFL debut.

events.name: Jack Buckley
events.note: Signed a three-year contract extension (the first multi-year deal of his career) to remain at GWS through the end of 2026, about eight weeks after returning from a serious knee injury.

events.name: Jack Buckley
events.note: Signed a new four-year contract extension, adding to his existing 2026 deal to commit to GWS through the end of the 2030 season.

events.name: Aliir Aliir
events.note: Aliir signed a three-year contract extension with Sydney, tying him to the club through the end of 2021; Head of Football Tom Harley confirmed the deal.

events.name: Aliir Aliir
events.note: Aliir requested a trade from Sydney to Port Adelaide, who sent a future second-round pick to the Swans; he signed a four-year deal at Port Adelaide as part of the move.

events.name: Aliir Aliir
events.note: Aliir signed a two-year contract extension with Port Adelaide, keeping him at the club until at least the end of 2026.

events.name: Aliir Aliir
events.note: Aliir triggered a one-year contract extension ahead of the 2026 season, tying him to Port Adelaide until the end of 2027.

events.name: Shannon Neale
events.note: Neale was one of five young Cats to sign a contract extension, tying him to Geelong through the end of 2023.

events.name: Shannon Neale
events.note: Neale and James Willis recommitted to Geelong, with Neale signing a two-year extension to remain at the club until the end of 2025.

events.name: Shannon Neale
events.note: Neale signed a three-year extension alongside Jeremy Cameron and Ollie Henry, committing to Geelong until at least the end of 2028.

events.name: Shannon Neale
events.note: Neale signed a two-year contract extension, committing to Geelong until at least the end of 2030; this is his current active deal.

events.name: Charlie Curnow
events.note: Curnow signed a four-year contract extension with Carlton, committing to the club until at least the end of 2023.

events.name: Charlie Curnow
events.note: Fresh off his first Coleman Medal, Curnow signed a six-year contract extension with Carlton, tying him to the club until the end of 2029, turning down a reported seven-year rival offer.

events.name: Charlie Curnow
events.note: Sydney won the race for Curnow on the final day of the 2025 trade period, sending Will Hayward and first-round picks in 2025, 2026 and 2027 to Carlton in return for the two-time Coleman Medallist plus picks 31, 42 and a 2027 second-round selection.

events.name: Connor Rozee
events.note: Rozee and teammate Zak Butters both signed two-year contract extensions with Port Adelaide, tying them to the club through to the end of the 2024 season.

events.name: Connor Rozee
events.reporter: Port Adelaide FC / ESPN AFL / Zero Hanger
events.note: Rozee was appointed Port Adelaide captain and signed an eight-year contract extension, the club's biggest-ever deal, committing him to the Power until the end of 2032.

events.name: Paul Curtis
events.note: Curtis signed a three-year contract extension with North Melbourne, committing to the club until at least the end of 2028; he was previously contracted through 2025.

events.name: Paul Curtis
events.note: Curtis signed a five-year extension keeping him at North Melbourne through at least 2033, having previously been committed until 2028; the club's head of football talent Brady Rawlings praised him as a key part of the Roos' young forward crop. Exact announcement date could not be confirmed from the source and was estimated to mid-2026.

events.name: Jake Soligo
events.note: Soligo, previously contracted through the end of 2025, signed a four-year contract extension with Adelaide keeping him at the club through the 2029 season.

events.name: Sam Switkowski
events.note: Signed a contract extension during the 2022 season (after recovering from a Round 13 back injury) keeping him at Fremantle through the end of 2024.

events.name: Sam Switkowski
events.note: Signed a two-year contract extension, adding to his previous 2024 deal and committing him to Fremantle through the end of the 2026 season.

events.name: Angus Sheldrick
events.note: Sheldrick signed a two-year contract extension with the Swans, tying him to the club until at least the end of 2025 (reported in a Sydney Swans article about Nick Blakey's own extension, which noted Sheldrick had 're-signed earlier this season').

events.name: Angus Sheldrick
events.note: Sheldrick agreed to a two-year contract extension keeping him at Sydney through the end of 2027, resisting interest from other clubs including West Coast, after establishing himself as a regular AFL midfielder.

events.name: Josh Battle
events.note: Battle, then 19, re-signed with St Kilda on a two-year deal after completing Year 12, his first re-signing since being drafted in 2016 (exact date not stated in source, estimated to mid-2018).

events.name: Josh Battle
events.note: Battle signed a two-year contract extension with St Kilda, securing him through the end of 2024; also reported by AFL.com.au ("Battle won: Defender re-signs") and saints.com.au ("Battle ready for future at Saints").

events.name: Josh Battle
events.note: Battle left St Kilda after eight seasons/123 games and joined Hawthorn as an unrestricted free agent on a six-year deal through the end of 2030; St Kilda received band-one free agency compensation (pick 8, 2024 draft).

events.name: Mabior Chol
events.note: Richmond delisted Chol at the end of the 2018 season; GM Neil Balme said the club would not offer him a new contract.

events.name: Mabior Chol
events.reporter: Wikipedia (citing Fox Sports rookie draft live coverage)
events.note: After being delisted, Chol was re-drafted by Richmond with pick 45 in the 2019 (Nov 2018) rookie draft, restarting his AFL career at the same club.

events.name: Mabior Chol
events.note: At the end of the 2021 season Chol exercised free agency and left Richmond to join Gold Coast; the Suns lodged free agent paperwork with the AFL.

events.name: Mabior Chol
events.note: With two years still to run on his Gold Coast contract, Chol requested a trade; Hawthorn acquired him (plus pick 62) for a future 2nd-round pick and signed him to a new four-year deal.

events.name: Jamie Elliott
events.note: Pre-listed by expansion club Greater Western Sydney as one of 10 players in an AFL deal to on-trade players to other clubs for draft picks; as part of that deal Elliott was traded to Collingwood at the end of 2011 before playing a game for GWS.

events.name: Jamie Elliott
events.note: Re-signed with Collingwood for another year, reported 1 October 2018.

events.name: Jamie Elliott
events.note: Reported as set to sign a new Collingwood deal despite hamstring surgery affecting his pre-season; exact signing date not confirmed by the source, so date is estimated to early 2019.

events.name: Jamie Elliott
events.note: Signed a three-year extension with Collingwood, keeping him contracted through the end of 2025; Collingwood GM of Football Graham Wright: "We're pleased to extend Jamie for another three years."

events.name: Jamie Elliott
events.note: Committed to finishing his career at Collingwood, signing a new deal on the Wednesday before the Magpies' 2025 preliminary final loss to Brisbane; exact calendar date not confirmed in available excerpts, so estimated to mid-September 2025. Contract length/end year not disclosed in accessible reporting.

events.name: Darcy Wilmot
events.note: Wilmot, then contracted until end of 2025, signed a two-year extension (alongside Kai Lohmann) keeping him at Brisbane until at least the end of 2027; announced September 2023.

events.name: Darcy Wilmot
events.note: Wilmot, already contracted until end of 2027, signed a further two-year extension keeping him at Brisbane until at least the end of 2029; announced 8 December 2025.

events.name: Max Hall
events.note: Hall signed a two-year contract extension with St Kilda, keeping him at the club until at least the end of 2027, after breaking out as one of the surprise packets of the 2025 AFL season following his mid-season draft selection in 2024.

events.name: Will Ashcroft
events.note: Ashcroft signed a four-year contract extension with Brisbane, keeping him at the club through the end of 2030; the deal came after his second consecutive Norm Smith Medal and Brisbane's back-to-back premierships.

events.name: Harry Sheezel
events.note: Sheezel signed a four-year contract extension with North Melbourne, keeping him at the club until at least the end of 2030; he had previously been contracted through 2026.

events.name: Harry Sheezel
events.note: North Melbourne vice-captain Sheezel added a further two years onto his previous deal, locking him in with the Kangaroos through the end of 2032.

events.name: Kieren Briggs
events.note: Briggs signed a new two-year contract with GWS, extending his deal through the end of the 2024 season, after stringing together a run of senior games late in 2022.

events.name: Kieren Briggs
events.reporter: AAP / Canberra Times, corroborated by Zero Hanger
events.note: After a breakout 2023 season and his first finals appearance, Briggs signed a two-year extension with GWS, keeping him at the club through the end of the 2026 season.

events.name: Riley Thilthorpe
events.note: Thilthorpe, originally contracted through 2022 as the No.2 pick in the 2020 draft, signed a three-year contract extension with Adelaide, committing him to the club until the end of 2025.

events.name: Riley Thilthorpe
events.note: Already contracted through 2025, Thilthorpe signed a further three-year extension with Adelaide, taking his deal through to the end of the 2028 season (when he will become a free agent).

events.name: Gryan Miers
events.note: Signed a new three-year contract extension with Geelong, keeping him at the club until at least the end of 2026; announced on the eve of his 100th AFL game against Essendon.

events.name: Gryan Miers
events.note: Signed a two-year contract extension with Geelong, committing to the club until at least the end of 2028; signed a year before he would have become a free agent.

events.name: Tom Atkins
events.note: Atkins signed a two-year contract extension with Geelong, keeping him at the club until at least the end of 2027; he had been eligible for free agency at season's end but chose to re-sign.

events.name: Darcy Cameron
events.note: Traded from Sydney to Collingwood (with pick 62) in exchange for pick 56 during the 2019 trade period, after requesting a move to Victoria for more senior opportunity; joined the Magpies on a two-year contract.

events.name: Darcy Cameron
events.note: Signed a fresh three-year contract extension with Collingwood, committing him to the club through the end of 2025.

events.name: Darcy Cameron
events.note: Signed a one-year contract extension alongside teammates Patrick Lipinski and Finlay Macrae, pushing his deal out to the end of 2026.

events.name: Darcy Cameron
events.note: With one year remaining on his existing deal (through 2026), signed a new three-year extension keeping him at Collingwood through the end of 2029; reportedly turned down interest from West Coast to re-sign.

events.name: Shaun Mannagh
events.note: Mannagh signed a contract extension with Geelong keeping him at the club until at least the end of 2026.

events.name: Shaun Mannagh
events.reporter: Geelong Cats (official) / Geelong Independent / Zero Hanger
events.note: Mannagh signed a three-year contract extension, keeping him at Geelong until the end of the 2029 season.

events.name: Jason Horne-Francis
events.note: Horne-Francis was traded from North Melbourne to Port Adelaide in a four-club mega trade (also involving West Coast and GWS), joining Port on a six-year deal running until the end of 2028.

events.name: Jason Horne-Francis
events.note: As part of his move, Horne-Francis signed a six-year contract with Port Adelaide, listed as contracted until the end of 2028; this remains his active deal as of mid-2026 with no confirmed further extension found (an April 2026 AFL.com.au video titled 'Port's pay rise, mega deal for Horne-Francis' hints at extension talk but no signed terms could be verified).

events.name: Jeremy Cameron
events.note: Cameron signed a five-year contract extension with GWS, keeping him at the club through to the end of 2020, heading off interest from Victorian clubs including Carlton.

events.name: Jeremy Cameron
events.note: After Cameron requested a move as a restricted free agent and Geelong's bid went unmatched, GWS traded him to the Cats on the final day of the 2020 trade period for a package of draft picks; he signed a five-year deal with Geelong.

events.name: Jeremy Cameron
events.note: Cameron signed a two-year contract extension with Geelong, keeping him at the club until at least the end of 2027.

events.name: Josh Treacy
events.note: Treacy signed a three-year contract extension with Fremantle, committing through the end of the 2026 season.

events.name: Josh Treacy
events.note: Treacy signed a further four-year extension with Fremantle, taking his contract through to the end of the 2030 season, alongside forward teammates Luke Jackson and Jye Amiss also being re-signed long-term.

events.name: Oliver Dempsey
events.note: Dempsey signed a four-year contract extension with Geelong, keeping him at GMHBA Stadium through the end of 2029, off the back of his 2024 AFL Rising Star-winning season.

events.name: Kade Chandler
events.note: Chandler signed a three-year extension with Melbourne, committing him to the club through the end of the 2026 season.

events.name: Kade Chandler
events.note: Chandler turned down free agency and re-signed with Melbourne for a further five years, committing to the club until the end of 2031.

events.name: Josh Ward
events.note: Ward signed a two-year contract extension with Hawthorn, keeping him at the club until at least the end of 2025, after a strong debut season and Rising Star nomination.

events.name: Josh Ward
events.note: Ward signed a four-year contract extension with Hawthorn, taking him through to free agency at the end of 2029.

events.name: Matthew Kennedy
events.note: Traded from GWS to Carlton with less than an hour remaining in the 2017 AFL trade period, in exchange for selection 28; GWS had not offered him a new contract.

events.name: Matthew Kennedy
events.note: Re-signed with Carlton on a new one-year deal, keeping him at the club through the end of 2022 (exact publication date not shown on page; dated via related SEN coverage from April 27, 2022).

events.name: Matthew Kennedy
events.note: Extended his contract with Carlton for three more years, taking him through to the end of 2025, on the back of career-best form.

events.name: Matthew Kennedy
events.note: Traded from Carlton to the Western Bulldogs in the dying minutes of the 2024 trade period, as part of a four-club, three-player deal also involving Bailey Smith (to Geelong) and Jack Macrae (to St Kilda); Carlton received pick 38. New contract length/end year with the Bulldogs was not publicly disclosed by either club.

events.name: Josh Dunkley
events.note: Signed a two-year contract extension with the Western Bulldogs, keeping him at the club through the end of the 2019 season.

events.name: Josh Dunkley
events.note: Re-signed with the Western Bulldogs alongside Caleb Daniel for a further three years, locking him in until the end of 2022.

events.name: Josh Dunkley
events.note: Traded from the Western Bulldogs to the Brisbane Lions on the final day of the 2022 AFL Trade Period, after requesting a move; the Bulldogs received a first, second and fourth-round future selection plus pick 21.

events.name: Josh Dunkley
events.note: Signed a six-year contract with the Brisbane Lions on joining the club as part of the trade from the Western Bulldogs, running from the 2023 season.

events.name: Josh Dunkley
events.note: Signed a two-year contract extension with Brisbane, taking him to the end of 2030, following his first Merrett-Murray Medal (2025) and appointment as Lions co-captain for 2026.

events.name: Dayne Zorko
events.note: As club captain, Zorko re-signed with Brisbane to keep him contracted until the end of 2022.

events.name: Dayne Zorko
events.note: Zorko, an unrestricted free agent, signed a one-year contract extension keeping him at Brisbane for a 12th season in 2023.

events.name: Dayne Zorko
events.note: Signed a new one-year deal to play on for a 13th season in 2024, off the back of a Grand Final campaign.

events.name: Dayne Zorko
events.note: Signed a one-year deal for a 14th season, keeping him at Brisbane through the end of 2025.

events.name: Dayne Zorko
events.note: Signed a one-year contract extension ahead of his 300th AFL game, keeping him at Brisbane for a 15th season through 2026.

events.name: Jack Steele
events.note: Signed a two-year contract extension with St Kilda, tying him to the club until at least the end of 2022.

events.name: Jack Steele
events.note: Dual All-Australian and Saints co-captain signed a fresh five-year contract extension, committing to St Kilda until the end of 2027.

events.name: Jack Steele
events.note: Traded from St Kilda to Melbourne on deadline day of the AFL Trade Period for a future third-round selection; his contract was extended by an added year as part of the move, locking him in at the Demons until the end of 2028.

events.name: Joel Freijah
events.reporter: Western Bulldogs official website / Zero Hanger
events.note: As a first-year AFL player (drafted pick 45, 2023), Freijah signed a one-year contract extension with the Western Bulldogs, taking his deal through the end of the 2026 season.

events.name: Joel Freijah
events.note: Freijah signed a three-year contract extension with the Western Bulldogs, keeping him at the club through the end of the 2029 season; announced alongside teammate Rhylee West's own extension.

events.name: Toby Greene

events.name: Toby Greene

events.name: Trent Rivers

events.name: Darcy Fort

events.name: Callum Wilkie

events.name: Jordan Clark

events.name: Cam Rayner

events.name: Cam Rayner

events.name: Josh Rachele

events.name: Josh Daicos
events.note: Signed a two-year contract extension with Collingwood after his 2018 season, alongside Brody Mihocek.

events.name: Josh Daicos

events.name: Josh Daicos

events.name: Sam Darcy
events.note: Re-signed with the Western Bulldogs on a two-year extension, keeping him at the club until the end of 2025.

events.name: Sam Darcy

events.name: Luke Parker

events.name: Jordon Sweet

events.name: Jordon Sweet

events.name: Jordon Sweet

events.name: Scott Pendlebury

events.name: Scott Pendlebury

events.name: Scott Pendlebury
events.reporter: Wikipedia, citing Eddie McGuire's Copeland Trophy announcement
events.note: Collingwood president Eddie McGuire announced at the Copeland Trophy that Pendlebury had re-signed with the club through the end of 2020.

events.name: Scott Pendlebury
events.note: Pendlebury signed a two-year extension, taking him into an 18th AFL season and through the end of 2023.

events.name: Scott Pendlebury

events.name: Scott Pendlebury

events.name: Scott Pendlebury

events.name: Dylan Moore

events.name: Dylan Moore

events.name: Dylan Moore

events.name: Dylan Moore

events.name: Dylan Moore

events.name: Sam Collins

events.name: Sam Collins

events.name: Sam Collins

events.name: Sam Collins

events.name: Harley Reid

events.name: Ben Keays
events.note: Delisted by Brisbane along with Josh Walker and Ryan Bastinac after four seasons and 30 games; told he would not be offered a contract for 2020.

events.name: Ben Keays
events.note: Picked up by Adelaide with selection 7 in the 2019 AFL rookie draft after being delisted by Brisbane; exact draft-day date used as estimate.

events.name: Ben Keays

events.note: Signed a two-year extension in October 2021 to remain at Adelaide until the end of 2024; club GM Justin Reid praised his reliability and leadership qualities.

events.name: Ben Keays
events.reporter: Adelaide FC (afc.com.au) - "Ben Keays' journey from a Lion to Crows Vice Captain"
events.note: Signed a new three-year deal shortly after being appointed Crows vice-captain ahead of the 2024 season, keeping him at Adelaide through 2027.

events.name: Jake Bowey
events.note: Bowey signed a contract extension with Melbourne through the end of the 2028 season, announced by the club on 16 December 2025 following a 2025 season in which he averaged 22 disposals and finished fourth in Melbourne's best and fairest.

events.name: Liam Baker
events.note: Baker signed a two-year contract extension with Richmond, keeping him at the club through the end of the 2024 season.

events.name: Liam Baker
events.note: Baker was traded from Richmond to West Coast in a three-way deal also involving Carlton (which sent Matt Owies to West Coast), fulfilling his wish to return home to Western Australia. events.name: Mason Redman

events.name: Jack Macrae

events.name: Jack Macrae

events.name: Sam Berry
events.note: Berry signed a two-year contract extension with Adelaide, taking him through to the end of the 2026 season. Exact within-month announcement date is not stated on the source page, so late-August 2024 is used as an estimate based on surrounding news timing.

events.name: Lloyd Meek
events.note: Traded from Fremantle to Hawthorn along with a 2023 second-round pick, in exchange for Jaeger O'Meara moving to Fremantle. No contract length was disclosed.

events.name: Jack Ross

events.name: Jack Ross

events.name: Jack Ross

events.name: Patrick Dangerfield
events.note: Re-signed with Adelaide for three years following his breakout 2012 season, a deal well received by Crows supporters.

events.name: Patrick Dangerfield

events.name: Patrick Dangerfield

events.name: Patrick Dangerfield

events.name: Hugo Garcia

events.name: Wayne Milera

events.name: Wayne Milera

events.name: Wayne Milera
events.note: Re-signed with Adelaide on a three-year extension, locking him in until the end of the 2028 season. Was previously out of contract at the end of 2025; the deal extends his tenure with the club to 13 years (also reported by Zero Hanger).

events.name: Jy Simpkin
events.note: Signed a two-year contract extension (his first re-sign, three games into his debut season) taking him to the end of 2020. Article references 'last week's' Good Friday loss to the Western Bulldogs (14 Apr 2017), so exact publish date is estimated to late April 2017.

events.name: Jy Simpkin

events.name: Jy Simpkin
events.note: New deal signed 19 Oct 2021 (per embedded tweet timestamps), extending him to the end of 2024, shortly after his first Syd Barker Medal win; also covered by AFL.com.au (afl.com.au/news/685202).

events.name: Jy Simpkin

This remains his current, active contract; he was heavily linked with a trade to Collingwood in the 2025 trade period but North Melbourne rejected offers and he stayed at the club under this contract, losing the captaincy afterward. Also reported by AFL.com.au (afl.com.au/news/933099) and Zero Hanger (zerohanger.com/north-co-captain-jy-simpkin-signs-new-long-term-deal-137833).

events.name: Joel Jeffrey

events.name: Ryley Sanders

events.name: Dan Houston

events.name: Karl Amon

events.name: Sam Draper

events.note: Signed a two-year contract extension, tying him to North Melbourne until the end of 2024, amid interest from rival clubs.

events.name: Cameron Zurhaar
events.note: Signed a five-year contract extension, keeping him at North Melbourne until at least the end of 2029, having been headed for free agency; cited teammates Simpkin, Larkey, Xerri and Sheezel re-signing as an influence.

events.name: Jaxon Prior
events.note: Re-signed with Brisbane Lions for a further two years, taking him through to the end of 2024. Corroborated by AFLRATINGS contract update dated the same day (aflratings.com.au/2022/09/28/contract-update-jaxon-prior/).

events.name: Jaxon Prior
events.note: Delisted by Brisbane Lions after 39 games across five seasons; club footy manager Danny Daly called it a 'tough decision'.

events.name: Jaxon Prior
events.note: Signed by Essendon on the opening day of the Supplemental Selection Period (SSP), linking him with the club his father Michael played 81 games for. Contract length not disclosed in reporting; also covered by AFL.com.au (afl.com.au/news/1258987) and 7News.

events.name: Jaxon Prior
events.note: One-year contract extension keeping Prior at Essendon through the 2027 season; article ('Prior on board for 2027') is undated on-page, estimated mid-July 2026 based on search-result recency (~3 weeks before Aug 3 2026). GM Matt Rosa: Prior has 'become an important member of our group'.

events.name: Judd McVee
events.note: Signed a two-year contract extension with Melbourne (his original club), tying him to the Demons until at least the end of 2025.

events.name: Judd McVee
events.note: Traded from Melbourne to Fremantle for pick 23 in the 2025 AFL Draft on day three of the trade period, in a deal that also involved West Coast. McVee was out of contract at Melbourne and had requested a trade home to Western Australia (see also https://aflratings.com.au/2025/10/08/judd-mcvee-joins-fremantle/ and https://www.afl.com.au/news/1433660/melbourne-demons-defender-judd-mcvee-makes-trade-request-wants-move-home-to-western-australia-and-fremantle-dockers).

events.name: Judd McVee
events.note: Signed a five-year contract with Fremantle upon his trade from Melbourne, running through the end of the 2030 season. Also reported by Midwest Times: 'Geraldton's Judd McVee reflects on his decision to return home after signing five year deal with Fremantle' (https://www.midwesttimes.com.au/news/midwest-times/geraldtons-judd-mcvee-reflects-on-his-decision-to-return-home-after-signing-five-year-deal-with-fremantle--c-20401796). Exact signing date not separately confirmed from the trade date, so estimated as coinciding with the October 8, 2025 trade.

events.name: Tyson Stengle
events.note: Traded from Richmond to Adelaide during the 2018 trade period in exchange for Adelaide's 4th-round selection (pick 68). Exact day of the trade not stated in source; October 2018 trade period used as month anchor.

events.name: Tyson Stengle
events.note: Delisted by Adelaide on 17 March 2021 after he declined a conditional offer restricting him to SANFL following a string of off-field indiscretions.

events.name: Tyson Stengle
events.note: Signed with Geelong as a delisted free agent on a reported two-year deal after starring at SANFL level for Woodville-West Torrens in 2021. Exact signing date (5 Nov 2021) sourced from Wikipedia; length/end_year inferred as 'two-year deal' reported in press coverage, not confirmed on this primary article.

events.name: Tyson Stengle
events.note: Signed a one-year (12-month) contract extension on 10 February 2023, committing him to Geelong until at least the end of the 2024 season, following his breakout 2022 premiership/All-Australian season.

events.name: Tyson Stengle
events.note: Signed a five-year extension on 30 June 2024, committing him to Geelong until the end of 2029 as an unrestricted free agent who fielded interest from rival clubs (reportedly including St Kilda). This deal was terminated early — see the 2026-07-31 delisting event — so it is not the current contract.

events.name: Tyson Stengle
events.note: Geelong and Stengle reached a mutual agreement to terminate his contract on 31 July 2026, despite three years remaining on his 2024 five-year extension, after he played only one VFL game in 2026 amid off-field issues and had not featured at AFL level since the 2025 Grand Final loss. He finished with 93 games and 160 goals for Geelong. As of this research he has no AFL club contract, so no event is marked current=true; he has not been reported as retired.

events.name: Anthony Caminiti
events.note: Undrafted forward Caminiti (training at Carlton in the VFL) was added to St Kilda's list via the pre-season Supplemental Selection Period (SSP), days before the Feb 15 deadline, after key forwards Max King, Jack Hayes and Matt Allison were injured. Corroborated by SEN (archive.sen.com.au, dated 2023-02-14, 'How a "crazy", "whirlwind" week ended in St Kilda list spot for Blues trainee').

events.name: Anthony Caminiti
events.note: Signed a three-year contract extension tying him to St Kilda through the end of 2026, after kicking 9 goals in his first 6 AFL games off the back of his SSP signing. Date confirmed via matching SEN report published 2023-05-18 (sen.com.au/news/2023/05/18/...-the-incredible-rise-of-re-signed-saint).

events.name: Anthony Caminiti
events.reporter: Callum Twomey, Riley Beveridge & Josh Gabelich, AFL.com.au
events.note: Report ('Inside Trading') revealed St Kilda had quietly reworked/extended Caminiti's deal beyond its original 2026 expiry some time earlier; he is now contracted for a fifth season at Moorabbin, through the end of 2027 (58 games played, now used across both forward and defensive ends). Exact rework/announcement date not stated in the article, hence estimated to mid-2026 based on the article's position in AFL.com.au's Inside Trading series timeline (published between late-June and early-August 2026 dated companion pieces).

events.name: Oliver Hollands
events.reporter: Nick Austin (Carlton List Manager) / Zero Hanger, Carlton FC
events.note: Ahead of his Round 1 2023 AFL debut vs Richmond, Hollands (pick 11, 2022 draft, originally on a 2-year rookie deal covering 2023-2024) signed a 2-year contract extension with Carlton, taking him through to the end of 2026. Corroborated by Carlton FC's own report 'Round 1 debutants pen contract extensions' (https://www.carltonfc.com.au/news/1282141/round-1-debutants-pen-contract-extensions) and by Zero Hanger's current player profile (https://www.zerohanger.com/afl/players/oliver-hollands/) which still lists him 'Contracted Until 2026' as of the research date (Aug 2026) - no later re-signing was found despite extensive searching across club news, AFL.com.au, ESPN AFL, SEN, Zero Hanger, AFLRATINGS, Wikipedia and Blueseum. The original 2022 mandatory draft contract is omitted as a separate event per instructions since he has since re-signed.

events.name: Oisin Mullin
events.note: Signed a contract extension keeping him at Geelong until at least the end of the 2025 season, after an impressive debut AFL campaign in 2023. AFL.com.au's report on the same deal ('Irish Cat inks extension after impressive debut campaign', https://www.afl.com.au/news/1062336/irish-cat-oisin-mullin-inks-extension-after-impressive-debut-campaign) describes it as a one-year extension to the same end date (undated on the AFL.com.au page itself, hence using the dated Irish Times report of the same news); exact length is ambiguous between sources (reported variously as one- or two-year) but the resulting expiry (end of 2025) is consistent across both.

events.name: Oisin Mullin
events.note: Re-signed with Geelong for a further two years, extending his contract until at least the end of the 2027 season. This is his current active deal (confirmed no newer extension as of Aug 2026, per his own comments in July 2026 that he turned down a Mayo GAA approach to stay committed to Geelong).

events.name: Sam Banks
events.note: Signed a two-year extension alongside fellow 2021 draftees Judson Clarke and Tom Brown, tying him to Richmond through the end of 2025 after 17 VFL games in his first year.

events.name: Sam Banks
events.note: Signed a two-year extension through 2027 after a breakout 2025 season at half-back (25.6 disposals/game across the prior five weeks; 33 AFL games played at time of signing).

events.name: Dylan Stephens
events.note: Recommitted to Sydney for 'a further two seasons' after being linked with a trade amid the club's salary-cap squeeze; extension ran through end of 2023. Corroborated by AFL.com.au 'Hands Off' article and Sydney Swans' 'Swans quartet commit' piece (both undated, same news cycle).

events.name: Dylan Stephens
events.note: Traded from Sydney to North Melbourne; Swans received a future first-round pick (2024) plus pick 44 (2023), North Melbourne sent out picks 21 and 25. Trade paperwork approved 11 Oct 2023 per @AFLHouse, cited by Wikipedia.

events.name: Dylan Stephens
events.note: Signed a four-year deal with North Melbourne concurrent with the trade, running through end of 2027. This remains his current, active contract as of the 2026 season (no subsequent re-signing found despite targeted searches for a 2025/2026 extension).

events.name: Karl Worner
events.note: One-year rookie contract extension, keeping Worner at Fremantle through the end of the 2023 season (also announced by the club as 'Karl Worner extends!').

events.name: Karl Worner
events.note: Two-year contract extension (announced around his 21st birthday) keeping Worner at Fremantle until the end of the 2025 AFL season.

events.name: Karl Worner
events.note: Two-year contract extension tying Worner to Fremantle until at least the end of the 2027 AFL season; his current active deal.

events.name: Dane Rampe
events.note: Announced May 2015 (exact day not confirmed): four-year extension keeping the then-24-year-old at Sydney until the end of the 2019 season.

events.name: Dane Rampe
events.note: Announced December 2018 (a Gold Coast Bulletin/Pressreader report dated 2018-12-08 covers the same deal but could not be fetched directly): three-year extension taking Rampe to at least the end of 2022, signed roughly a year ahead of what would have been free agency. Corroborated by sydneyswans.com.au/news/43359/rampe-re-signs.

events.name: Dane Rampe
events.note: One-year extension on top of the 2018 three-year deal, taking Sydney co-captain Rampe (then 31) through to the end of the 2023 season. Also reported by AFL.com.au as 'Off the table: Co-captain Dane Rampe turns back on free agency to stay a Swan' (afl.com.au/news/702974).

events.name: Dane Rampe
events.note: Two-year extension signed 21 June 2023, keeping the then-33-year-old co-captain at Sydney through the end of the 2025 season; he had been slated to become an unrestricted free agent. Also covered by sydneyswans.com.au/news/1362111/rampe-commits-to-the-sydney-swans.

events.name: Dane Rampe
events.note: Delisted by Sydney ahead of the 2025 National Draft as a list-management/salary-cap mechanism, with the club publicly committing to re-draft him via the Rookie Draft. Also reported by AFL.com.au (afl.com.au/news/1444498) and Zero Hanger (zerohanger.com/sydney-delist-veteran-duo-with-draft-intent-170313).

events.name: Dane Rampe
events.note: Re-drafted by Sydney through the 2025 Telstra AFL Rookie Draft (held 21 Nov 2025) after being delisted, on what SEN reported as a one-year deal for the 2026 season -- his current, active contract. Also covered in sydneyswans.com.au/news/1922070/dane-rampe-and-jake-lloyd-to-go-again.

events.name: Joe Fonti
events.note: Two-year contract extension announced 6 Sep 2024, taking Fonti (drafted pick 44, 2023) from his existing 2025 contract through to the end of the 2027 season. Corroborated by Zero Hanger (https://www.zerohanger.com/giants-make-call-on-veterans-future-youngster-commits-154838/) and confirmed as his current contract by his Zero Hanger player profile listing 'Contracted Until: 2027' (https://www.zerohanger.com/afl/players/joe-fonti/). His original mandatory draft contract (2024-2025) is omitted per instructions since he has since re-signed. No later re-signing was found despite searching through 2026.

events.name: Jake Melksham
events.note: Two-year contract extension with Essendon, keeping him at the club through the end of the 2015 season.

events.name: Jake Melksham
events.note: Traded from Essendon to Melbourne for pick No.25 during the 2015 NAB Trade Period.

events.name: Jake Melksham
events.note: Signed a three-year contract extension with Melbourne, keeping him at the club until the end of 2022.

events.name: Jake Melksham
events.note: One-year contract extension alongside Michael Hibberd, taking him into a seventh season at the club (through 2023).

events.name: Jake Melksham
events.note: Delisted by Melbourne as part of first list lodgement, with the club committing to re-select him via that year's AFL Rookie Draft; he was recovering from a late-season ACL injury.

events.name: Jake Melksham
events.note: Re-selected by Melbourne with pick 12 in the 2023 AFL Rookie Draft after being delisted, securing what became his 15th AFL season while he recovered from ACL surgery.

events.name: Jake Melksham
events.note: One-year deal through the 2025 season, marking a decade as a Demon, after his comeback from ACL reconstruction.

events.name: Jake Melksham
events.note: One-year extension through the 2026 season, following a career-high 33-goal campaign in 2025. This is his current active contract.

events.name: Mitchell Hinge
events.note: Delisted by Brisbane Lions (originally pick 20, 2017 rookie draft, from Glenelg) after just 3 games in four seasons; signed by Adelaide as a delisted free agent on a two-year deal ahead of the 2021 season, rejecting a one-year offer to stay at Brisbane.

events.name: Mitchell Hinge
events.note: Signed a two-year contract extension during the 2022 season, keeping him at Adelaide until the end of 2024 (also reported by the club at afc.com.au/news/1194031/hinge-signs-on).

events.name: Mitchell Hinge
events.note: Signed a contract extension ahead of the 2024 season, taking his deal through to the end of 2026 (at least three more seasons at the time). This is his current, active contract; he appears on the AFL's official list of 2026 free agents (delisted-free-agent eligible), meaning no further extension has been reported as of August 2026.

events.name: Brady Hough
events.reporter: West Coast Eagles official website / BigFooty Contracts Thread
events.note: Signed a 3-year contract extension (covering 2026-2028) on his existing contract that was due to expire at the end of 2025, announced in August 2024 alongside teammate Harry Edwards ('Harry and Houghy locked in'). Confirmed by BigFooty Contracts Thread: 'Brady Hough (5/3/03) - Signed a 3 year extension (2026-28) on an existing contract due to expire 2025 in August 2024.' Exact day of announcement not stated in source; month/year confirmed by multiple sources.

events.name: Lachlan Cowan
events.note: Extended his original 2-year rookie deal (2022 draft, pick 30) by two additional seasons, taking him through the end of 2026.

events.name: Lachlan Cowan
events.note: Re-signed alongside fellow young defenders Matt Carroll and Harry O'Farrell (both to end of 2027); extended from his prior end-of-2026 deal by two more years to the end of 2028. Current active contract.

events.name: Buku Khamis
events.note: Category B rookie Khamis re-signed for the 2021 season, his third year at the club after joining via the Next Generation Academy pathway at the end of 2018.

events.name: Buku Khamis
events.note: Signed a one-year contract extension to remain at the club for the 2022 season; 21-year-old defender in his third AFL season.

events.name: Buku Khamis
events.note: One of a trio of Bulldogs (with Mitch Hannan and Dom Bedendo) to sign a one-year extension, keeping him contracted for the 2023 season; corroborated by AFLRATINGS' 22 June 2022 contract-updates post for Western Bulldogs.

events.name: Buku Khamis
events.note: Signed a fresh one-year deal to stay for the 2024 season despite having played only one AFL game in 2023; announced 'on Friday' per SEN's 7 Oct 2023 follow-up piece (dated to the preceding Friday, 6 Oct 2023).

events.name: Buku Khamis
events.note: Signed a two-year extension through 2026 after a breakout season (17 games) in the backline. This remains his active deal: he requested a trade to Carlton in September 2025 (agreeing to a 3-year Carlton offer) but the move fell through at the Oct 2025 deadline when Carlton ran out of trade capital, so he stayed at the Bulldogs on this contract; he is set to become an unrestricted free agent at the end of 2026 (see afl.com.au recap).

events.name: Luke McDonald
events.note: Re-signed with North Melbourne through the end of 2018.

events.name: Luke McDonald
events.note: Signed a new three-year deal with North Melbourne; McDonald: "I'm stoked to be here the next three years and hopefully longer." Exact expiry year not stated in source; inferred as 2021 (2019-2021).

events.name: Luke McDonald
events.note: Signed a five-year contract extension on the eve of the 2021 season (ahead of free agency eligibility), keeping him at North Melbourne until the end of 2026. Reigning Syd Barker medallist at the time.

events.name: Luke McDonald
events.note: AFL.com.au 'Inside Trading' column (Twomey/Gabelich/Beveridge) reported the Kangaroos were 'finalising a one-year extension with McDonald after 17 appearances in 2026', setting him up for a 14th AFL season in 2027. Exact signing/announcement date not stated by source, estimated to mid-2026 based on '17 appearances in 2026' context; deal described as being finalised rather than confirmed complete at time of reporting.

events.name: Tom Papley
events.note: As a first-year rookie (20 years old, 11 games into his debut season), Papley signed a two-year contract extension with Sydney. Exact signing date not stated in the source; year/month inferred from context (mid-2016, his debut season).

events.name: Tom Papley
events.note: Signed a two-year contract extension (reported alongside a teammate, hence 'Young duo locked in') during the first week of pre-season training in the 2017 off-season, keeping him at Sydney until at least the end of 2020. Exact date not given; estimated to mid-November 2017 based on typical pre-season start.

events.name: Tom Papley
events.note: Signed a five-year contract extension confirmed 30 September 2022, committing to Sydney through end of 2028. He moved early - his prior deal wasn't due to expire until end of 2023 (avoiding entering free agency). Papley had earlier requested a trade to Carlton at the end of 2019, but that trade did not eventuate and he remained at Sydney throughout; this is his current, active contract. Corroborated by https://www.afl.com.au/news/852534/sydney-swans-star-tom-papley-signs-five-year-deal-avoids-free-agency and https://archive.sen.com.au/news/2022/09/30/papley-moves-early-to-sign-long-term-contract-with-swans/index.html

events.name: Harrison Petty
events.note: Signed a 2-year contract extension beyond his mandatory rookie deal (which ran to end of 2019), locking him in until the end of 2020. Reported jointly with fellow 2017 draftees Bayley Fritsch and Charlie Spargo under the headline 'Good news comes in threes for Dees'. Petty had not yet made his AFL debut at this point.

events.name: Harrison Petty
events.note: Signed a fresh 3-year deal to the end of 2025 off the back of his 2021 premiership season (19 games including the Grand Final, filling in after Adam Tomlinson's ACL injury), despite already being contracted through 2022 on a prior deal. Same signing also reported at afl.com.au/news/685835 and via Zero Hanger (zerohanger.com/premiership-demon-inks-long-term-deal-melbourne-afl-petty-93202).

events.name: Harrison Petty
events.reporter: Zero Hanger (citing Channel 9's Tom Morris) / Melbourne FC Media
events.note: Signed a fresh extension keeping him at Melbourne until the end of 2027, turning down interest from home-state club Adelaide (one rival reportedly offered two first-round picks). List manager Tim Lamb described it as Petty 'signing on for another three seasons'. Confirmed by the club in a joint announcement with Caleb Windsor, 'Petty and Windsor put pen to paper' (melbournefc.com.au/news/1608935). This is his current, active contract.

events.name: Callum Ah Chee
events.note: Traded from Gold Coast to Brisbane Lions at the end of the 2019 AFL season; Gold Coast received a future round-2 2020 selection. Source is Wikipedia's Ah Chee page, which cites an AFL House tweet dated 16 Oct 2019 for the trade.

events.name: Callum Ah Chee
events.note: Brisbane and Adelaide could not agree a trade during the 2025 trade period, so Ah Chee (uncontracted, requested move to be closer to family roots after Brisbane's 2025 flag) nominated for the Pre-Season/Rookie Draft and was taken with pick 1 by Adelaide on a 2-year deal reported at over $1M/season. Draft date estimated from Wikipedia's 2025 AFL draft key-dates page (Pre-Season and Rookie draft held 21 Nov 2025); Brisbane received no compensation.

events.name: Callum Ah Chee
events.note: Ah Chee added three years onto his original 2-year pre-season-draft contract, rounding out to the full five-year deal (through 2030) Adelaide had originally offered him before the 2025 trade period. Reported in AFL.com.au's 'Inside Trading' column; exact publish date not shown in fetched content, estimated from in-article references to 2026 Round 21.

events.name: Logan Evans
events.note: Signed a three-year contract extension to remain at Port Adelaide until at least the end of 2028, roughly a year after being drafted with pick 12 in the 2024 AFL mid-season rookie draft (debuted weeks after selection). Corroborated by Zero Hanger (https://www.zerohanger.com/port-adelaide-success-story-pens-new-deal-162657/), which dates the deal to 20 May 2025. This is his current active contract; no other re-signing found, so the original mid-season-draft rookie contract is omitted per instructions since it has been superseded.

events.name: Hayden McLean
events.note: Re-signed by Sydney after his debut 2019 season (he joined as a pre-season rookie/supplemental selection out of South Australia in March 2019), extending his contract through the 2020 season.

events.name: Hayden McLean
events.note: Signed a four-year contract extension to remain at Sydney until the end of 2027, announced following the 2023 AFL season; club article gives no exact date so the 15th (mid-October, typical re-signing window) is used as an estimate.

events.name: Lachlan McNeil
events.note: Two-year contract extension signed early in his debut season (after being drafted with pick 11 in the 2020 AFL Rookie Draft), tying him to the Western Bulldogs 'until the end of 2023'.

events.name: Lachlan McNeil
events.note: Delisted at the end of his 2023 contract and immediately re-drafted by the Western Bulldogs (with Taylor Duryea) via the AFL Rookie Draft, held ~2 days after that year's National Draft. Exact date and contract length are estimated from context; length/end_year inferred as a standard 1-year rookie deal, superseded by the Sept 2024 extension below.

events.name: Lachlan McNeil
events.note: Two-year contract extension announced 11 September 2024, running through the end of 2026. Independently corroborated by Zero Hanger's player profile, which lists him as 'Contracted Until 2026'. This is his current active deal as of Aug 2026; no evidence found of any further extension since.

events.name: Zac Taylor
events.note: One-year contract extension with Adelaide, taking him through to the end of 2026. Originally reported by AFC ('Young Crows pair sign on', 19 Sep 2025) and corroborated by AFLRATINGS and Wikipedia; this is his current active deal. His original contract was the mandatory deal from being drafted at pick 44 in the 2021 AFL Draft.

events.name: Jye Amiss
events.note: Amiss signed a six-year contract extension with Fremantle during the 2023 season, tying him to the club until at least the end of 2029 - a major commitment for the then-20-year-old key forward. Corroborated by a Fremantle FC (fremantlefc.com.au) article from August 2024 covering Josh Treacy's extension, which lists Amiss alongside Luke Jackson as already 'locked in for the long haul' through 2029.

events.name: Jayden Laverde
events.note: Extended at Essendon on a three-year deal through the end of 2025, having played 73 games for the Bombers at the time.

events.name: Jayden Laverde
events.note: Delisted by Essendon after 145 games (2015-2025), then joined GWS through the pre-season Supplemental Selection Period on a one-year contract; GWS EGM Jason McCartney praised him as a proven, physical defender.

events.name: Tim Membrey
events.note: Delisted by Sydney after 2014 season; announced he would join St Kilda as a delisted free agent when the free agency period opened, effective for the 2015 season. Exact signing date not stated in source; estimated to the free agency period opening.

events.name: Tim Membrey
events.note: Became eligible for the 'free agency for life' clause in 2021 (delisted by a club previously) but instead signed a new three-year contract with St Kilda through the end of 2024. Article followed his 3-goal, 21-disposal performance vs GWS in Round 1, 2021 (played March 21, 2021); exact signing/publication date estimated from that context.

events.name: Tim Membrey
events.note: Delisted by St Kilda at the end of the 2024 season after 178 games and 293 goals across a decade at the club, to allow the club to expose young forwards to more senior opportunities. Exact date per secondary summary; not independently confirmed on the page itself.

events.name: Tim Membrey
events.note: Signed by Collingwood as a delisted free agent on a two-year contract, taking him through to the end of the 2026 AFL season. Signed on/around the opening of the AFL's delisted free agency period; exact date not stated on the page itself.

events.name: Jake Waterman
events.note: Per Wikipedia body text: 'In September, Waterman signed a two-year contract extension' with West Coast, taking him through the end of the 2025 season. Primary source (The West Australian, 21 Aug 2024 article referencing this) could not be directly fetched (site blocked); citing Wikipedia's sourced summary instead.

events.name: Jake Waterman
events.note: Signed a new deal on 9 Oct 2024 extending his commitment to West Coast through the end of 2029, reportedly worth approx. $1M/season; he was already contracted through 2025 at the time (from the Sept 2023 two-year extension). Waterman: 'locked away here for the next five years.' This is his current active contract.

events.name: Bruce Reville
events.note: One-year contract extension signed after his 2024 debut season (12 games, missed finals). Quote: "It's massive to know I'm going to be here another year and can solely focus on my footy." Exact publish date not shown on page; estimated as shortly after the 2024 home-and-away season based on Wikipedia's account that the extension followed his missing Brisbane's 2024 finals series.

events.name: Bruce Reville
events.note: Three-year contract extension through end of 2029, announced jointly with teammate Zane Zakostelsky, following Reville's role in Brisbane's 2025 premiership. Quote: "It feels amazing to re-sign and it means so much for me and my family – so it was one of the easiest decisions I have ever had to make." Exact publish date not shown on page; estimated mid-2026 based on Wikipedia's account that this occurred "during the 2026 AFL season" and FootyWire stats context (through Round 20, 2026).

events.name: Corey Durdin
events.note: Signed a two-year contract extension with Carlton, keeping him at the club through the end of the 2026 season. Carlton head of list management Nick Austin praised his dynamic small-forward play; corroborated by AFLRATINGS (https://aflratings.com.au/2024/05/02/corey-durdin-car/).

events.name: Corey Durdin
events.note: Traded from Carlton to Port Adelaide on Day 5 of the 2025 Trade Period in a three-club deal (Carlton also gained Ben Ainsworth and pick 67 from Gold Coast; Port Adelaide sent its 2026 2nd-round pick to Carlton and pick 29 to Gold Coast). Per SEN (https://www.sen.com.au/news/2025/10/14/afl-2025-why-corey-durdin-chose-port-adelaide), Durdin had one year left on his Carlton contract (his May-2024 extension, expiring end of 2026) at the time of the trade, which transferred with him to Port Adelaide -- end_year is inferred from that, not separately quoted for the Port deal. Also reported by AFL.com.au: https://www.afl.com.au/news/1439517/gold-coast-suns-small-forward-ben-ainsworth-traded-to-carlton-blue-corey-durdin-joins-port-adelaide

events.name: Darcy Parish
events.note: Signed a 2-year extension keeping him at Essendon until the end of 2021, off the back of a career-best 2019 season.

events.name: Darcy Parish
events.note: Signed a further 2-year deal, committing to Essendon until the end of 2023, after a breakout 2021 season averaging 32 disposals.

events.name: Darcy Parish
events.note: Rejected restricted free agency to re-sign with Essendon. Initially announced by the club as a deal to 'at least the end of 2028' (reported by most outlets as 5 years); it was clarified in late October 2023 that the actual term is 6 years, running to the end of 2029 (see ESPN and Nine.com.au follow-up coverage of the length discrepancy).

events.name: Jack Viney
events.note: Three-year contract extension linking Viney to Melbourne until the end of the 2020 season.

events.name: Jack Viney
events.note: Turned down free agency interest (incl. Geelong) to re-sign with Melbourne on a five-year deal through the end of the 2025 season.

events.name: Esava Ratugolea
events.note: Signed a two-year contract extension with Geelong, running through the end of 2023, ahead of his 50th AFL game.

events.name: Esava Ratugolea
events.note: Traded from Geelong to Port Adelaide during the 2023 trade period, with Port Adelaide sending picks 25, 76 and 94 to Geelong. He was out of contract at the end of 2023 (restricted free agent) and requested the move; exact length/value of his new Port Adelaide contract was not publicly disclosed. He remains at Port Adelaide as of mid-2026 (sidelined most of that season after knee surgery), so this is his current club.

events.name: Sean Darcy
events.note: Signed a six-year contract extension with Fremantle, tying him to the club until the end of 2030. Previously contracted only through 2024 and slated to become a Restricted Free Agent; had played 98 games at time of signing. Corroborated by Wikipedia's citation to the original Fox Sports (foxsports.com.au) report of the same date, and by AFLRATINGS' news-aggregator page for Darcy which shows no other contract events before or after.

events.name: Isaiah Dudley
events.reporter: Fremantle Football Club / National Indigenous Times
events.note: One-year contract extension (with Aiden Riddle) keeping Dudley on Fremantle's rookie list through the end of the 2026 season. Confirmed by NIT (published 2025-06-12) and consistent with Zerohanger's player profile showing 'Contracted Until: 2026'. His original entry to the club was via the pre-season Supplemental Selection Period in Feb 2025 (signed as replacement for injured Odin Jones) - skipped as an event per instructions since he has since re-signed.

events.name: Isaiah Dudley
events.note: Dudley activated a games-based trigger clause in his contract, automatically extending his deal to the end of the 2027 season, after playing all nine games to that point in the 2026 season. Independently confirmed by AFL.com.au's 'Inside Trading' column (www.afl.com.au/news/1502832/inside-trading-lions-bailey-plans-dog-lands-new-deal-dockers-livewire-hits-trigger), which states he 'hit a trigger for a new deal at the Dockers for 2027.' Exact trigger date not published, so the Fox Sports report date (2026-05-11) is used as an estimate.

events.name: Jackson Mead
events.note: Signed a two-year contract extension, taking him through to the end of 2024. Reported via AFLRATINGS 'Contract Updates: Port Adelaide' post; exact signing date not stated, article date used as estimate.

events.name: Jackson Mead
events.note: Signed a two-year extension following his breakout 2024 season, keeping him at Port Adelaide until the end of 2026. This is his current active contract (no re-signing beyond 2026 has been found as of Aug 2026, despite having played 9 games in 2026 through Round 20).

events.name: Harry Sharp
events.note: Signed a two-year contract extension with Brisbane, tying him to the club until at least the end of 2025. Quote from the article: 'YOUNG Brisbane winger Harry Sharp has signed a two-year contract extension, tying him to the club until at least the end of 2025.'

events.name: Harry Sharp
events.note: Traded from Brisbane to Melbourne for pick 49 plus an exchange of future picks; AFL.com.au reported 'The Demons have signed Sharp' as part of the deal, but did not publish a contract length. No dedicated re-signing article was found despite extensive searching (AFL.com.au search, Melbourne FC site search, Brisbane Lions site, Bing/DuckDuckGo web searches for many query variants). end_year of 2026 is corroborated by Zero Hanger's live off-contract tracker: Sharp appears on the 2026 off-contract list (https://www.zerohanger.com/afl/players/off-contract-2026/) and is absent from the 2027 list, confirming his current Melbourne contract runs through the end of 2026 but not stating an exact signing date, hence end_estimated=true.

events.name: Nate Caddy
events.note: Signed a two-year contract extension, taking him through to the end of the 2028 season. Announced at the NEC Hangar; quote: "it's super exciting and rewarding to be offered the two-year contract extension."

events.name: Nate Caddy
events.note: Re-signed with Essendon through to the end of 2031, extending his prior deal (which ran to end of 2028) by a further three years. List manager Matt Rosa called it 'a powerful statement of belief in this footy club'; Caddy: 'Committing until the end of 2031 was an easy decision for me.' This is his current active contract.

events.name: Rhys Stanley
events.note: Traded from St Kilda to Geelong (Geelong sent pick 21 for Stanley and pick 60) during the 2014 trade period, after 58 games with the Saints over six seasons. Exact trade-period date not stated in the source; October 2014 used as a plausible estimate.

events.name: Rhys Stanley
events.note: Signed a two-year contract extension alongside fellow ruckman Ryan Abbott ('Cats shore up ruck stocks, re-sign quartet'). Article has no visible publish date/byline timestamp; contextual clues (Abbott's Round 20 debut already having occurred) place it around August 2018, so both date and end_year are estimated.

events.name: Rhys Stanley
events.note: Signed a two-year extension to remain at Geelong until the end of 2023, part of a five-player Geelong re-signing round ('New deals for Cats five'), taking him to his eighth season at the club. URL confirmed via Wikipedia's citation (accessed by Wikipedia editors 30 Sep 2022); the krockfootball.com.au domain now 301-redirects to a generic K Rock Football hub page due to site restructuring, but the citation itself is genuine, not fabricated.

events.name: Rhys Stanley
events.note: Signed a one-year extension through the end of 2025, announced alongside teammates Patrick Dangerfield (2-year extension to 2026) and Mitch Duncan (1-year to 2025). His 11th season at the club. Also confirmed by Geelong FC ('Cats trio resigns', geelongcats.com.au/news/1686713) and K Rock Football.

events.name: Rhys Stanley
events.note: Signed a one-year extension through the end of 2026 alongside young midfielder Mitch Knevitt ('Cats secure Stanley and Knevitt for 2026'), his 12th season with the club. Confirmed by football boss Andrew Mackie; also reported by K Rock Football and Zero Hanger, both dated 9 October 2025. This is his current active contract.

events.name: Brody Mihocek
events.note: Re-signed a two-year extension with Collingwood, tying him to the club through the end of 2025 (165 goals/102 games at time of signing). Article language ('ahead of Christmas') places this in December 2022 but no exact date is published, so the date is estimated.

events.name: Brody Mihocek
events.note: Unrestricted free agent Mihocek moved from Collingwood to Melbourne via a trade brokered on day 5 of the 2025 Trade Period (Mihocek + Pick 71 to MEL; Pick 61 + a 2026 3rd-round pick to COL) rather than a straight free-agency signing, so both clubs could preserve compensation-pick value elsewhere. Zero Hanger reports he signed a two-year deal with Melbourne; the exact 2027 expiry is inferred from the reported length, not stated explicitly in the source.

events.name: Koltyn Tholstrup
events.note: AFLRATINGS' living news page for Tholstrup states verbatim: 'Koltyn Tholstrup has signed a two-year contract extension (via Melbourne)', dated 26 Jul 2024. No explicit expiry year is quoted in the source, so end_year is estimated as signed-year + length (2024+2=2026) per this project's existing contracts.py convention; it is plausible the true expiry is 2027 if the 2-year extension was layered on top of his still-running 2-year rookie deal (drafted pick 13, 2023) rather than replacing it. The page has been continuously updated by AFLRATINGS through 18 Jul 2026 (injury/selection items added as recently as that date) with no further contract event logged, so this extension is treated as his still-current deal. The original mandatory draft signing (pick 13, 2023 draft, 20 Nov 2023, also documented on the same page) was skipped per instructions since he has since re-signed once.

events.name: Mitch Georgiades
events.note: First re-signing: after his 2020 debut season (7 games, Rising Star nomination Rd 9), Georgiades signed a contract extension keeping him at Port Adelaide through the end of 2023, alongside fellow 2019 draftees Miles Bergman and Dylan Williams. Exact byline date not readable on the page; year/period inferred from the debut-season context described in the article, so date is estimated.

events.name: Mitch Georgiades
events.reporter: Port Adelaide FC (official) / Ryan Daniels, Channel 7 (via SEN)
events.note: Signed a four-year extension to remain at Alberton through the end of 2027, while sidelined with a season-ending ACL injury (ruptured April 2023) and previously due to become a free agent. Channel 7's Ryan Daniels broke the news via SEN on 2023-08-30 (https://archive.sen.com.au/news/2023/08/30/report-georgiades-inks-new-deal-to-remain-at-port-adelaide/index.html); official club confirmation followed within days -- treat date as approximate within the 2023-08-30 to 2023-09-04 window. Companion quotes piece: https://www.portadelaidefc.com.au/news/1423296/georgiades-this-club-is-pretty-special-to-me-its-like-a-big-family. IMPORTANT CAVEAT: as of early Aug 2026, multiple outlets (Fox Sports, SEN, 7News, ozbrief.com.au, and a Triple M/Chris Dittmar report via the 'We Are Port Adelaide' Facebook page) were reporting from mid-July 2026 that Georgiades was 'set to sign' or had verbally agreed to a further short-term (~2-year) extension beyond 2027. I could not reach a fetchable primary source confirming an actual signed deal with a firm date/length (Fox Sports, 7News, Sporting News and the Courier-Mail are blocked to this tool; the ozbrief and SEN 2026-07-14 article URLs both 404'd on retry), so no separate event was fabricated for it. AFLRATINGS' own live contract tracker (https://aflratings.com.au/afl-news-mitch-georgiades/, last touched with a 2026-07-11 note) still listed his status as 'signed through end of 2027' at last check. Recommend re-checking in a few weeks once an official club or AFL.com.au article confirms the new deal.

events.name: Jamie Cripps

events.name: Jamie Cripps
events.note: Two-year extension announced alongside Jeremy McGovern, Jack Petruccelle and Jack Williams, tying Cripps to West Coast until the end of 2025; corroborated by The West Australian and Zero Hanger the same week.

events.name: Jamie Cripps
events.note: Signed a one-year contract extension to remain at West Coast for the 2026 season (his 14th at the club), after being reported in August 2025 as on track for a fresh deal. This was his final playing contract before retiring mid-2026 — not marked current because he has since retired.

events.name: Jamie Cripps
events.note: Announced his retirement ('Cripps calls time') after 16 AFL seasons (14 at West Coast) — 277 career games, 339 goals (323 for West Coast), 2018 premiership player, West Coast Life Member. Retired mid-way through his one-year 2026 contract due to a knee injury; corroborated by AFLRATINGS (2026-07-01) and SEN.

events.name: Brayden Fiorini

events.note: Signed a two-year contract extension through to the end of 2025 after being linked to Collingwood in the 2022 trade period; coach Stuart Dew and the club worked to retain him ahead of his eighth AFL season. Exact signing date not disclosed in reporting; month/day estimated from trade-period timing referenced as 'last year's trade period' in a 2023 follow-up article.

Contract length/years with Essendon not publicly disclosed in reporting found; this is his current, active deal.

Exact date estimated as Feb 24 2025 (paperwork lodged the preceding Friday, announcement delayed to the following Monday for Strachan to inform teammates).

Date estimated from Zero Hanger's June 19 2025 report of the same deal (https://www.zerohanger.com/adelaide-ssp-ruckman-pens-new-deal-164066/); AFC article itself is undated. events.name: Cooper Lord
events.note: One-year contract extension to the end of 2026, following his selection with pick 9 in the 2024 AFL Mid-Season Rookie Draft and his Round 23, 2024 debut against West Coast. Also covered by Carlton FC (carltonfc.com.au/news/1716143/the-inside-scoop-lord-remains-in-navy-blue).

events.name: Cooper Lord
